changes.title: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search combining vector and full text for more relevant search results
changes.detail: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports hybrid search that combines vector similarity search with full-text search within a single query. By combining semantic meaning and exact term matching into a single ranked list of results, hybrid search captures both intent and precise terms for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agent memory, and search applications. This can deliver more relevant ranked results than either method alone. Hybrid search works with the same S3 Vectors APIs and maintains subsecond latency for infrequent queries and latency around 100 milliseconds or less for frequent queries. S3

changes.title: AWS KMS now supports key sharing with AWS Resource Access Manager
changes.detail: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now integrates with AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM), giving you a simpler and more consistent way to share KMS keys across your AWS accounts, within your organization in AWS Organizations, and with specific IAM roles and users. You can now let trusted parties define the access they need through reusable managed permissions in RAM, while keeping full control of your keys and key policies. changes.title: AWS Secrets Manager adds managed external secrets support for Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks
changes.detail: AWS Secrets Manager now supports managed external secrets for Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks. Long-lived credentials that are not rotated increase the risk of unauthorized access if exposed. Rotating a third-party credential requires coordinated updates to the external service and every application that uses it. You set a rotation schedule from the AWS Management Console or API. Secrets Manager rotates the credential and stores the current value without a custom rotation Lambda function. changes.title: IAM Identity Center now supports VPC endpoints and network access controls
changes.detail: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports interface VPC endpoints powered by AWS PrivateLink and network access controls, enabling you to keep IAM Identity Center traffic private and restrict which networks can reach your IAM Identity Center services. Previously, IAM Identity Center rejected traffic arriving through VPC endpoints, requiring all sign-in and API traffic to use public endpoints. With this launch, you can create interface VPC endpoints for AWS access portal and service APIs to route traffic over the AWS private network. changes.title: AWS announces Networking Flexible Cost Allocation for Amazon VPC
changes.detail: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) now supports Networking Flexible Cost Allocation (FCA), which splits shared networking costs by the resources that actually drive them, so you can see what each team or application used. Until now, AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR), including CUR 2.0 in AWS Data Exports, showed networking usage as a single item, and most customers split it across teams with custom scripts and manual estimates.
